details: Peter Toma in 1968, is one of the oldest machine translation companies. SYSTRAN has done extensive work for the United States Department of Defense and the European Commission. SYSTRAN provided the technology for Yahoo! Babel Fish until May 30, 2012, among others. It was used by Google's language tools until 2007. SYSTRAN is used by the Dashboard Translation widget in macOS. Commercial versions of SYSTRAN can run on Microsoft Windows (including Windows Mobile), Linux, and Solaris. Historically, SYSTRAN systems used rule-based machine translation (RbMT) technology. With the release of SYSTRAN Server 7 in 2010, SYSTRAN implemented a hybrid rule-based/statistical machine translation (SMT) technology which was the first of its kind in the marketplace. As of 2008, the company had 59 employees of whom 26 are computational experts and 15 computational linguists. The number of employees decreased from 70 in 2006 to 59 in 2008. In January 2024, ChapsVision acquired Systran.

explainer.lead: SYSTRAN is one of the oldest machine translation companies, founded by Dr. Peter Toma in 1968. It matters because its technology reached the US Department of Defense, the European Commission, and consumer web tools.

tiers.eli5: It's one of the original translation machines: it has been turning text from one language into another since long before phones could do it.
tiers.practitioner: Commercial SYSTRAN versions run on Microsoft Windows (including Windows Mobile), Linux, and Solaris. Its technology powered Yahoo! Babel Fish until May 30, 2012, and Google's language tools until 2007.
tiers.paperLevel: A machine translation system and product line dating to 1968, delivered as commercial software across several operating systems. Limits: it is a translation system, not a general-purpose model.

explainer.example: Yahoo! Babel Fish used SYSTRAN technology for its translations until May 30, 2012.
